_comment: THE EXIT EXECUTOR'S MCP SURFACE — DECLARED, NEVER INHERITED.
Used with `claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config deploy/exit_mcp.json`,
which ignores the user/global MCP config entirely.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until now the exit executor was spawned with no MCP
flags at all, so it inherited the USER-level config in /root/.claude.json
— every claude.ai account connector the human who codes on this box has
ever connected. That is the same inheritance that killed the 10:35 open
session on 2026-08-13 by context-thrashing, and deploy/session_mcp.json
closed it for the trading sessions while leaving it wide open here.
⛔ AND IT IS WORSE ON THIS PATH THAN IT WAS ON THAT ONE. The connectors
reachable that way include OTHER BROKERS with live trading surfaces —
Interactive Brokers, webull, Public.com. A stop-triggered, headless,
live-money process had them mounted. Nothing is known to have called one:
the permission allowlist never named them. But CLAUDE.md's first hard rule
is that execution happens ONLY through Robinhood and ONLY in the Agentic
account, and a rule enforced solely by an allowlist that nobody re-derives
when a connector is added is a rule waiting to be edited by accident. Under
strict mode those servers are not merely forbidden, they are ABSENT.
ONE SERVER, deliberately. prompts/exit.md reaches the broker over MCP and
everything else over Bash (`.venv/bin/python scripts/record_*.py`), so the
agentic-trader server the trading sessions use is not needed here and is
not mounted — see deploy/exit_executor_settings.json for the full surface.
⛔ NO SECRETS HERE, AND NONE MAY BE ADDED. Robinhood is a remote HTTP MCP
whose OAuth lives in the CLI's own credential store, not in this file.
This file is committed.
